### 2026-10-24 – Okay sooo i started off with doing the Schematic for my pcb. It took me a bit to get into the groove of things and use kiCAD again however after figuring out the ESP pins and connecting up my board th

**2.5h**

Okay sooo i started off with doing the Schematic for my pcb. It took me a bit to get into the groove of things and use kiCAD again however after figuring out the ESP pins and connecting up my board things started to go smoother.

![0.5 HOURS](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/ae777d2eb3f37e1459db227d2e5b3c5f718f3f259619cf0c2dbafe573078781e.png)
This was me at 0.5 hours

After the ESP I added the Piezo discs alongside the components that go along with them (diodes and resistors)

![1 hr](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/ea919b8288ec89b1f50b92e71ce58478a586089476723ea900ae38a1a19fe6d2.png)

This was me around 45-50 mins in

![final schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/13b1ea29357ff57479176967cd2760ba360d565391f556a7ec2b18490c239129.png)

After this I added in the rest of my components ( the level shifter (as input is 3.3 V and the LED'S require 5V of power), the connector pins for the LED's, The amplifier module and the speaker)
This took around 20 mins and I was done around an hour and 30 minutes in , following this I ran the ERC(?) rules checker, some of these errors were corrected by making the speaker a passive component (editing footprint) and also fixing a typo ("Piezo 2 in" to "Piezo2 in") . The other errors are directly connected to the chaos covered below. EDIT- The speaker was in fact not fixed by me changing it to a passive component, the issue was once again in my naming conventions and spacing- I fix this after doing my PCB routing.

![errors](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/814ed95c60b5ad03860afd97f9942fa06c2755607607368a698835cd408a5de8.png)

THEN WHY IS THIS ENTRY 2 HOURS YA MAY ASK, well the reason for that is the imported symbol was for some reason slightly off, which kept resulting in

![1000163419](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/0ddaea3f2febef4f869bd01e27078fde9daf43642d41f6c143ba4d9dbb3d31cc.jpg)

![1000163417](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/2176bb9043a7267acdeab5f6d5c629473e5c27a17737f6bd4f416ac4f3fafaa7.jpg)

![1000163409](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/03eeb30f06fa49835e50ac6fdf41d6721bada5d4af7bea43767cc4589852a55d.jpg)

that the wires kept refusing to connect to the labels (which was odd because they were EXACTLY on the spots they were supposed to be at) however there was essentially no connection in the schematic, I tried to rewire a few times however that did not fix the issue in the slightest. This was when I realised that the issue was only on one side of the schematic- which led me onto my next course of action looking at the footprint of the schematic which led me to the realisation that all the GPIO pins which had issues had decimal x and y coordinates like so

![what i think is the issue](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/1b4e51f68f2781bd4793603271bb3fe426d87059c0a9470de3ef2e8332d3624c.png)

I observed the other side of the footprint which did NOT have decimal values and it was way better suggesting that this was the issue so I tried changing the values

![fixed it](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/4ec55ea3a80eb8de67a01cd823872205bb1dce3f6952714980ad3a5fcb09df6d.png)
like so for all of the erroneous pins which fixed my issue

![finally yay](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/6c2b6cbbc6e9a380c77f7afe3c79c7a3d68ad0ab665a07af7e397bbc80260b3f.png)
YAY FIXEDD

I largely did the troubleshooting off camera because I was unsure if it was genuinely an issue or a case of me being dumb ToT, it took wayyyyyyy longer than 15 mins however it was largely due to my own ignorance therefore, I will only claim 15.

After this I mainly just assigned footprints for everything.

![footprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/a8c7df84e560823b12c97a30754e2780780e0bbea61bd8aa9b9c3b757c5eb57a.png)
and kinda just stopped for the day now that I was done with my schematic.

tldr:- usual schematic stuff mostly except for the fact that my footprint decided to betray me ToT

### 2026-10-24 – Now that I was done with my schematic I started routing my pcb which started off with a minor issue aka the footprint for the aht 13 did not sync for some reason so I had to go fix that.

**1.12h**

Now that I was done with my schematic I started routing my pcb which started off with a minor issue aka the footprint for the aht 13 did not sync for some reason so I had to go fix that.

![WITHOUT AHCT125](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/ef73efd004f20ffee2e5f59f5f0c4254137d317eea03f90d635df246119a2d3c.png)
Missing version

![FIXED](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/98c5dceedac1239f508bc6ad20fd8f95e652bef04545f54bb3a3307f7970f721.png)
Fixed version

After this I arrange my components

![everything arranged](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/a95c90bdf034c16ce2c8485cc80820c8b646dd9e791e79089d88d3582003f6f7.png)
and started wiring them, wiring went smoothly almost suspiciously smoothly....

![wired 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/2842b299dcbbc8a90061919afbf448a4ec65c314a6171f79ae851a98658e0a1b.png)

I ran a DRC found no major errors except a fairly simple connection and was about to take my W when I noticed that wel............Piezo 3 and 4 had simply just disappeared from the ESP connections from my pcb diagram which is BADDD- I later realise this was because my footprint used GPIO numbers whereas my symbol used numbered pins from 1-16).
![drc1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/911e7fd921b606d30a2dd2b31940bc36441f61c2e8cef07e6a48de113d626882.png)

![missing Piezo's](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/e814cbba98c5d5fb8a053f13880962620f1e8bfdebe714d1c91676adbc2ac2f8.png)
 I found a different footprint using 1-16 which solved the issue however, that created

![mess](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/cee31602c57af836026908128d521046fa3dc7508b605ada0164efa9dacfa91f.png)

this mess.....I will fix it tomorrow and start with the firmware.

tldr- minor hiccups aside my pcb routing was going suspiciously well till I noticed...missing components and realised my footprint did not match my symbol, despite both being ESP32 C3 supermini which wel- lets just say was not ideal
